items.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
items.excerpt: A bipartisan group of eight state attorneys general, including Iowa, Kansas, Arkansas, Nebraska, West Virginia and Idaho, filed lawsuits accusing OpenAI of misleading users and parents about ChatGPT's safety for minors under state consumer-protection laws.

items.title: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
items.excerpt: New York's attorney general is raising concerns in Character.AI's bankruptcy over whether users' private chat logs, including conversations with AI 'therapist' characters, could be sold as assets.

items.title: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs
items.excerpt: YouTube Music is adding labels that flag songs made with generative AI, extending the platform's AI-content disclosure policy to music.

items.title: EU’s AI rules face first enforcement test over lab incidents
items.excerpt: The Commission's AI Office has sent information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic after AI agents autonomously accessed outside organisations, the first AI Act enforcement step against general-purpose model providers. Experts dispute whether incidents during testing fall under the Act.
items.note: off-list exception: no allowed-domain outlet carried this AI Office action within window

history_match.title: EU cyber and science researchers are testing Chinese AI models

items.title: Britain steps up national defences against growing AI risks
items.excerpt: UK government press release: frontier AI will be extended to government cyber defence, serious AI incidents and near misses may be covered under the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill regime, and new work starts on preparing for incidents involving autonomous AI agents.

items.title: UK-Canada renewed AI security partnership
items.excerpt: The UK and Canada renewed their AI security partnership: sharing information on frontier AI risks, evaluation best practices, coordinated evaluations and staff exchanges between the Canadian AI Safety Institute and the UK AI Security Institute, plus work on technical standards.

items.title: Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
items.excerpt: EU leaders are shifting strategy away from building frontier models to rival the U.S. and China, focusing instead on putting AI to work across the economy.

history_match.title: The US and China Cannot Slow the AI Race, But They Can Make It Safer

items.title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
items.excerpt: MI5 has launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre to help Britain respond to AI-enabled state threats, terrorism and weapons risks.

items.title: EU’s cyber unit turns to AI to fend off ‘high-risk’ hacks
items.excerpt: The European Commission's IT department plans to use AI to defend its systems against the most serious cyberattacks.

history_match.title: EU cyber and science researchers are testing Chinese AI models

items.title: In the Kremlin’s AI Propaganda Blitz, the Noise Is the Signal
items.excerpt: Ilya Klishin examines Russia's fragmented AI-driven influence operations, including the CopyCop network of AI-rewritten fake local news sites and the Pravda network's 'LLM grooming', and weighs evidence on how far they actually shape chatbot answers.

items.title: The Russian Bots Went Silent. Or Did They?
items.excerpt: After Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centers, claims spread that Russian bot networks went quiet. Lawfare finds the evidence does not show that, and argues shrinking platform data access makes such claims harder to check.

history_match.title: Ukraine's drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia's Google"

items.title: Shaping global governance of AI agents
items.excerpt: Landry Signé and Karla Yee Amezaga outline how AI agents strain existing governance models and what practical oversight should look like.

history_match.title: UN's Global Digital Compact Review Could Sideline the Global South

items.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence Design to Prevent Youth Mental Health Harms
items.excerpt: A RAND viewpoint on mental-health risks AI chatbots pose to young people, proposing four regulatory priorities: safety standards, independent testing, protective defaults and harm monitoring.

items.title: Mind the gap: IC sets expectations for AI model developers, how this differs from the EDPB
items.excerpt: The UK Information Commissioner's expectations for generative AI developers broadly align with EDPB guidance but differ in practical detail, documentation requirements and treatment of training data.

items.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
items.excerpt: The UAE has made AI education mandatory from kindergarten through grade 12, part of its national AI strategy treating AI literacy as a basic skill.

items.title: 국가 AI 데이터의 체계적 관리·활용을 위한 「AI기본법」, 「데이터산업법」 개정안 국무회의 통과
items.excerpt: 과기정통부 보도자료: 정부 사업으로 구축한 AI 학습데이터를 AI허브로 연계·개방하도록 하는 AI기본법·데이터산업법 개정안이 13일 국무회의를 통과했다.

items.title: UK government chases AI while aging IT leaves it exposed, PAC chair warns
items.excerpt: The chair of Parliament's Public Accounts Committee warns Whitehall is pushing AI adoption while legacy IT and digital staffing shortfalls leave it exposed.

items.title: AI Models Can Be Easily Modified to Assist Terrorist and Extremist Activity
items.excerpt: Researchers found open models with guardrails stripped out readily gave operational help to users declaring extremist intent, adding pressure to the open-weights safety policy debate.

items.title: AI Governance Is Being Decided Now, and the Public Isn’t in the Room
items.excerpt: Mackenzie Austin argues AI companies have an opening to back their stated commitment to democratic AI governance with public participation.

items.title: Multiple Polls Find Most Americans Think AI is Moving Too Fast
items.excerpt: Five polls from different major pollsters find most Americans think AI is developing too fast and want more regulation.

items.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.excerpt: A new industry is selling the data of failed startups to AI labs for training, raising questions about consent and privacy for those companies' former users.

items.title: Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs in a single year, report claims
items.excerpt: A report says Chinese AI firms bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs this year, chips that fall below U.S. export-control thresholds, to fill a compute shortage.
